CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: Sold-out products are not displayed on PLP by default
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Open a PLP with known sold-out SKUs in acceptance and compare visible item cards against stock state from business reference data.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
Sold-out SKUs are not visible on PLP by default.
No out-of-stock-only card appears in the first rendered product set.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: PLP keeps expected list size after sold-out filtering
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Use a PLP expected to render 100 products and confirm the rendered count after filtering sold-out items.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
Rendered product count remains 100 where 100 is the configured page size.
Filtering sold-out items does not reduce visible list size.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: Each filtered sold-out item is replaced by next available in-stock item
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Capture a before/after sample around positions where sold-out items would have appeared and verify in-stock replacements fill the gaps.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
No visual hole or reduced list length is present after filtering.
Replacement items are purchasable and in stock.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: Filtering behavior is consistent on NAP and MRP acceptance
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Run the same sold-out sample validation on both acceptance.net-a-porter.com and acceptance.mrporter.com.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
Both brands hide sold-out items by default.
Both brands maintain expected PLP page size after filtering.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: PLP remains stable during pagination or refresh when sold-out mix changes
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Refresh the PLP and navigate pagination where stock changes are likely, then verify no broken ordering block or empty slots appear.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
PLP remains visually stable after refresh/pagination.
No empty rows or rendering error state appears due to sold-out filtering.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: In-stock products remain discoverable after sold-out filtering logic
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Validate that expected in-stock SKUs still appear in PLP results and can be opened from product cards.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
In-stock SKUs are still visible and clickable.
Filtering logic does not remove valid in-stock products.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: Forced-visibility behavior is not used as pass/fail criterion for this epic
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Confirm business execution notes treat forced-visibility as out-of-scope and focus pass/fail on default sold-out filtering behavior.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
Execution notes clearly separate forced-visibility from this epic's acceptance checks.
Pass/fail decisions are based on default PLP stock filtering outcomes.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: PLP does not degrade when multiple sold-out products exist within the same result window
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Use a PLP window where several products are sold out and verify replacement still keeps page complete and purchasable.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
Multiple sold-out entries are filtered without UX degradation.
Replacement behavior still maintains complete purchasable PLP window.

MATRIX_ROWS.Capability: Default PLP result excludes sold-out products
MATRIX_ROWS.Evidence Notes: Directly mapped to acceptance criterion requiring out-of-stock exclusion from PLP.
MATRIX_ROWS.Inconsistencies: AC wording is broad and does not define edge-case handling by locale or category filter.

MATRIX_ROWS.Capability: PLP preserves configured result size by replacing filtered sold-out items
MATRIX_ROWS.Evidence Notes: Directly mapped to acceptance criterion stating the page remains at 100 items using next available products.
MATRIX_ROWS.Inconsistencies: Replacement tie-breaker order is not explicitly specified in story AC.

MATRIX_ROWS.Capability: Filtering logic does not create PLP rendering instability
MATRIX_ROWS.Evidence Notes: Derived from expected business usability of maintained list size and replacement behavior.
MATRIX_ROWS.Inconsistencies: No explicit AC sentence defines pagination/refresh behavior; inferred from outcome intent.

MATRIX_ROWS.Capability: In-stock visibility remains intact while sold-out items are filtered
MATRIX_ROWS.Evidence Notes: Supported by story intent to preserve purchasable-product experience while removing clutter from sold-out items.
MATRIX_ROWS.Inconsistencies: AC does not explicitly enumerate false-positive filtering risk for in-stock items.

MATRIX_ROWS.Capability: Forced-visibility behavior remains separate from this story's acceptance path
MATRIX_ROWS.Evidence Notes: Story explicitly marks forced visibility as out-of-scope and addressed separately.
MATRIX_ROWS.Inconsistencies: Future ranking implementation may reintroduce interactions requiring separate epic coverage.

MATRIX_ROWS.Capability: Outcome parity across NAP and MRP storefront acceptance environments
MATRIX_ROWS.Evidence Notes: Epic context targets both NAP and MRP customers; parity validation is required for business confidence.
MATRIX_ROWS.Inconsistencies: Story AC itself does not explicitly split acceptance by brand.

EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Summary: Replacement ordering logic for the next available product is not explicitly defined beyond keeping page size constant.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.How to Validate: Compare successive runs of the same PLP under similar data conditions and inspect whether replacement ordering remains stable and business-acceptable.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Expected Observation: Replacement behavior is consistent enough for merchandising expectations, even without a fully explicit tie-breaker in AC.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Evidence Notes: Derived from AC text and absence of tie-break details.

EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Summary: Legacy Gecco push-down behavior differs from Porter target hard-filter behavior and may surface migration regressions.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.How to Validate: Run side-by-side expectation review with product stakeholders for a sample PLP where multiple sold-out items existed in legacy behavior.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Expected Observation: Porter acceptance behavior follows hard-filter outcome and stakeholders confirm this as intended deviation from legacy.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Evidence Notes: Directly derived from story context section describing legacy versus target behavior.
